# Programming Fundamentals and OOP Laboratories

Compact laboratory modules for object-oriented modelling in Java 21 and explicit ownership in C++20.
The Java module models typed inventory containers; the C++ module implements a reference-counted
pointer and a tree with stable node addresses. There is no application to deploy: the public
contracts and their tests are the deliverable.

## Java inventory contracts

`Container` measures capacity in units rather than storage slots, retains immutable `Item` values,
and exposes an unmodifiable contents view. Its `label()` method supplies polymorphic rendering
without duplicating `toString()` in each subclass. Admission either takes a complete item or returns
`false`; callers retain control over any smaller split they want to make.

The Java tests exercise aggregate totals, order-independent admission, parsing choices, and subclass
rendering. This keeps domain rules executable instead of leaving them only in example output.

## C++ ownership and trees

`owning_ptr` uses separate specialisations for a single object and an array, so the allocation shape
and matching release operation are fixed by the type. Copy-and-swap assignment acquires the incoming
shared state before releasing the old state and also makes self-assignment safe. The type intentionally
does not promise thread safety.

The tree holds children through `std::unique_ptr`; growing the child vector moves pointers, not
nodes, so an accepted child address remains stable for that node's lifetime. `move_subtree` refuses
root, self, null, and descendant moves to preserve one rooted acyclic ownership tree. Explicit deep
copy keeps separate trees independent.

## Verification

On 2026-08-12, Java 21 Maven verification passed 27/27 tests. A fresh CMake C++20 build completed
with warnings treated as errors, and both native test binaries passed (2/2).

The C++ tests make lifetime observable with `tracked.hpp`, rather than requiring a sanitizer runtime
on every supported toolchain. Sanitizers remain an opt-in CMake check
(`-DFUNDAMENTALS_SANITIZE=ON`) and are an independent additional signal.

## Boundaries

These are deliberately small laboratory libraries, not a framework or an application. The tree tests
exercise representative structural cases; property-based generation is not part of the current suite.
Coursework provenance and the clean-room boundary are stated in the repository `NOTICE`.
